claims.claim: The main source of energy of the CNS is widely believed to be blood vessels/bloodstream supply.
The bloodstream cannot transport energy and can only carry substances that may participate in endergonic reactions.
Glucose is only a source of biomass rather than an energy provider.
Glycans have complex roles but function only as provision of essential metabolic intermediates and not as energy providers.
Any cell needs water not only as solvent/vehicle but as a fundamental chemical energy source.
Eukaryotic cells can dissociate water at room temperature to obtain energy.
Melanin in animals is analogous to chlorophyll in plants because both split/dissociate water.
“Human photosynthesis” is an appropriate analogy for melanin-mediated water splitting in humans.
Pharmacologic modulation of “human photosynthesis” offers efficient new treatments for several diseases.
Sugars are vital components influencing many cellular processes (cell-cell interactions, adhesion, signaling, clotting, blood types, development, structural roles).
When blood glucose falls to about 2–3 mM, cognitive impairment signs occur; below about 1 mM, confusion and coma may result with prolonged deprivation.
Peripheral tissues including muscle, fat, pancreas, and liver directly control transport, synthesis, storage, and metabolism of glucose.
Glucose cannot be considered the main energy provider of the human body and is instead only an indispensable metabolic intermediate.
Mitochondria are found in all human cells except mature erythrocytes.
Mitochondria generate ATP, which cells use for the majority of energy needs.
All organisms from bacteria to humans use ATP as their primary energy currency.
ATP is produced by one set of reactions and almost immediately consumed by another rather than stored long-term.
At any instant each cell contains about one billion ATP molecules and this suffices only for a few minutes, requiring rapid recycling.
Total human body ATP content is about 50 grams and must be constantly recycled every day.
A 2,500 kcal/day intake corresponds to about 180 kg/day ATP turnover and this is thermodynamically impossible.
Heart daily energy consumption is about 6 kg of ATP and exceeds other organs.
ATP breakdown to ADP absorbs more energy than it releases.
The prime function of the choroid plexus is to secrete CSF at about 0.4 ml/min in humans.
Total CSF volume is about 150–270 ml, with about 25% in ventricles and the remainder in basal cisterns/subarachnoid spaces.
Choroid plexus capillaries are fenestrated unlike cerebral capillaries, providing little resistance to small-molecule movement.
CSF is formed by active secretion rather than simple ultrafiltration, supported by ionic composition properties and homeostatic control.
The high energy requirement of CSF secretion cannot be fulfilled by ATP-based energy; water dissociation (“human photosynthesis”) makes it affordable.
The main source of energy of the human retina is water, not ATP.
Melanin can conduct at room temperature a biochemical reaction that in laboratory needs 2000 °C (water splitting).
“Human photosynthesis” is more efficient than plant photosynthesis because melanin absorbs energy through the whole electromagnetic spectrum while chlorophyll uses 400–700 nm.
In vegetables, the main source of energy is water because chlorophyll transforms solar energy into chemical energy by dissociating water.
Oxygen is a by-product of water dissociation that is toxic at any concentration.
Hydrogen is an energy carrier but not an energy resource and must be injected with energy because hydrogen itself has no energy.
In humans, water dissociation proceeds as 2H2O → 2H2 + O2 → 2H2O + 4e-.
Melanin absorbs any kind of energy, including gravitons, and uses absorbed energy mainly to dissociate water.
Abrupt reduction of “human photosynthesis” causes hemorrhage and edema; chronic reduction causes fibrosis and mitosis proportional to reduced water dissociation.
The cell nucleus has neither ATP nor mitochondria.
Nuclear energy needs are fulfilled by energy released through water dissociation (“human photosynthesis”).
Melanosomes tend to form an envelope around the nucleus, concentrating emanated energy into a high-energy center.
For every two molecules of water re-formed, four high-energy electrons are generated and shared easily.
Melanin maintains chemical energy within a stable range by decreasing excessive luminous energy and raising low luminous energy.
Melanin is the most stable molecule known, with stability evidenced over about 170 million years, and is likely the most stable molecule in the human body.
Mitochondria cannot explain energy stability because they appear/disappear and lack fixed intracellular placement.
If glucose were the energy source, diabetics would fly.
Nutrients provide building elements for biomolecules but not energy.
Increasing melanin-derived chemical energy makes tissues resistant to hypoxia/lack of circulation, including CNS.
Surgical management of cerebral vascular events produces severe sequelae, whereas QIAPI 1 treatment leaves no anatomic or functional sequelae.
Sublingual QIAPI 1 administered hourly for 6 hours reduced brain swelling by about 50% and restored consciousness and mobility.
No humans were used in the research and animal procedures followed the Guide for the Care and Use of Laboratory Animals (8th ed.).

concepts.definition: Extracellular fluid in ventricles and subarachnoid space supporting CNS buoyancy, protection, and chemical homeostasis.
Ventricular epithelial-vascular tissue producing most CSF via active ion transport and osmotic water movement.
Ion distribution across a semipermeable membrane influenced by impermeant charged species, yielding predictable concentration ratios.
Phosphoryl-transfer molecule coupling exergonic and endergonic reactions; hydrolysis provides free energy for cellular work.
Mitochondrial ATP synthesis driven by electron transport chain and proton motive force.
Broadband-absorbing redox-active biopolymer pigment (eumelanin/pheomelanin) present in skin, eye, and certain brain regions.
Organelle where melanin is synthesized and stored, especially in melanocytes and pigmented epithelia.
Light-driven oxidation of water to oxygen, protons, and electrons; biologically catalyzed in photosystem II.
Proposed melanin-mediated conversion of absorbed energy into chemical energy via water dissociation/reformation in humans.
Named agent claimed to intensify water dissociation and improve outcomes in cerebral vascular events.

logical_flow: Observation -> CNS energy is commonly attributed to blood-delivered substrates and mitochondrial ATP.
Interpretation -> Blood is treated as matter transport, not an energy carrier; glucose is reframed as non-energetic biomass/intermediate.
Mechanism -> Melanin absorbs ambient energy and dissociates water at physiological temperature, producing H2/O2 and then reforming water with electron release.
Distribution -> Hydrogen/electrons are asserted to distribute energy symmetrically through cytosol and nucleoplasm; perinuclear melanosomes concentrate energy for nuclear work.
Extension -> High CSF secretion energy demand is asserted to exceed ATP capacity and be met by water-dissociation energy.
Implication -> Pharmacologic enhancement of water dissociation is asserted to increase ischemia/hypoxia resistance and improve stroke outcomes compared with surgery.
Conclusion -> CNS physiology and treatment paradigms should be revised around melanin-driven water dissociation/reformation.
